title: Cookies
learning_outcomes: Explain what cookies contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: setting cookies.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: A web request carries a method, path, headers, and optional data; PHP uses these to produce a status, headers, and body. Keep HTTP details separate from application rules and templates. In this lesson, focus on setting cookies; then compare it with cookie expiration. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use cookies when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A web request carries a method, path, headers, and optional data; PHP uses these to produce a status, headers, and body. Keep HTTP details separate from application rules and templates. For cookies, begin with setting cookies. Also distinguish cookie expiration; cookie options; secure and httponly flags. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
